chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Admired musicians' habits and Thompson's early drinking
summary: He admired Waller, Calloway, Ellington and Hopkins as clean-cut, disciplined men, and says he was a professional drinker by 18.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: And as I said at this time there was Waller, Cab Calloway, Duke Ellington, Claude Hopkins. There's a difference between Claude Hopkins and Claude Thornhill, who comes later in my life. But they were all of these great musicians who looked up to and you admired

and you could learn from them. And they were mostly not only great and fine musicians, but believe it or not, even in those days most of these men were very intelligent type of people, clean cut people, well disciplined, well liked, dressed neat and had thousands of admirers. Because of their personal habits, which they didn't over exert themselves in these ways of, you know, deterioration of habits, you know.
And those who might have some bad habits, people had a tendency to kind of keep them a secret.

You know, people were ashamed to be seen, like even an alcoholic. Many musicians drink heavily, naturally because people are buying you drinks, and there were a lot of musicians who drank a lot of whiskey. In fact, by this time now, my age of 18, I was a professional drinker of alcohol.
Of course, because it was right there. I mean, how are you going to refuse it.
And it made you feel good. Alcohol makes you feel good. I don't care what nobody says, alcohol -- I've heard a lot of doctors say that alcohol is like medicine if you know how to handle it.
If you keep the right thing in your stomach. You know?
But it was all in fun.
